cards.heading: Core practice
cards.question: What does 'deletion confidence for dead code' treat a static analyzer's dead-code finding as?
cards.answer: A candidate, not a verdict — to be confirmed against dynamic evidence before deletion.

cards.heading: Static tool limitation
cards.question: Why can static dead-code tools produce false positives?
cards.answer: They examine source text without running it, so they can't see code reachable via metaprogramming, dynamic dispatch, or undeclared entry points.

cards.heading: Dynamic tool limitation
cards.question: What limits the trustworthiness of a dynamic (runtime-observation) 'unused' finding?
cards.answer: The length of the observation window — a path exercised once a quarter looks identically dead to a truly dead one until the tool has watched long enough to catch it.

cards.heading: Combined confidence rule
cards.question: When does this practice say it's safe to delete a flagged piece of code?
cards.answer: Only once static analysis flags it and a sufficiently long dynamic observation window has also failed to exercise it.

cards.heading: Sizing the observation window
cards.question: How should the dynamic observation window's length be chosen?
cards.answer: As a judgment call tied to the code's own usage cadence — e.g. quarterly billing logic needs a longer window than a request handler hit every second — not a fixed default.
